6	`datetime64` values.

freqs = ["Q-DEC","QE-DEC","QS-DEC","A-DEC","Y","AS-JAN","YS-JAN","M","ME","MS","7D","30D","3M","10D","D","h","2h","6h","min","S","2QS-OCT","2A-MAR","Q-JAN","Q-MAR","M-FEB" ]

mismatch = 0
n = 0
for periods in [1, 3, 40, 91, 365, 800]:

    for freq in freqs:
        for closed, label in [(None,None),("left","left"),("right","right")]:
            for cal in cals:
                for opt in data_options:
                    n += 1
                    if opt == "arange":
                        vals = np.arange(periods, dtype=float)
                    else:
                        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
                        vals = rng.random(periods); vals[::7] = np.nan
                    t_cf = pd_to_cf = None
                    import cftime
                    t_cf = [cftime.DatetimeNoLeap(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) if cal=="noleap" else
                            cftime.DatetimeAllLeap(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) if cal=="all_leap" else
                            cftime.Datetime360Day(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) if cal=="360_day" else
                            cftime.DatetimeJulian(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) if cal=="julian" else
                            cftime.DatetimeProlepticGregorian(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) if cal=="proleptic_gregorian" else
                            cftime.DatetimeGregorian(*pd.Timestamp(t).timetuple()[:6]) for t in t_pd]
                    # skip invalid calendar dates (all_leap/360_day may allow all; julian maps ok)
                    kw = {}
                    if closed: kw["closed"] = closed
                    if label: kw["label"] = label
                    da_pd = DataArray(vals, dims="time", coords={"time": t_pd})
                    da_cf = DataArray(vals, dims="time", coords={"time": ("time", t_cf)})
                    try:
                        r_pd = da_pd.resample(time=freq, **kw).mean()
                    except Exception as e:
                        continue  # pandas can't do some? should be fine
                    try:
                        r_cf = da_cf.resample(time=freq, **kw).mean()
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"MISMATCH-EXC periods={periods} freq={freq} cal={cal} closed={closed}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
                        mismatch += 1; continue
                    if r_pd.sizes["time"] != r_cf.sizes["time"]:
                        print(f"LEN-MISMATCH periods={periods} freq={freq} cal={cal} closed={closed}: pd={r_pd.sizes['time']} cf={r_cf.sizes['time']}")
                        mismatch += 1; continue
                    vpd, vcf = r_pd.values, r_cf.values
                    mask = ~(np.isnan(vpd) & np.isnan(vcf))
                    if not np.allclose(np.nan_to_num(vpd), np.nan_to_num(vcf)):
                        print(f"VAL-MISMATCH periods={periods} freq={freq} cal={cal} closed={closed}\n pd={vpd}\n cf={vcf}")
                        mismatch += 1; continue
                    # labels equivalent
                    lpd = pd.DatetimeIndex(r_pd["time"].values)
                    lcf = [str(t) for t in r_cf["time"].values]
                    lpds = [t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") for t in lpd]
                    lcf = [t.replace("T"," ").split(".")[0] for t in lcf]
                    lpds = [t.split(".")[0] for t in lpds]
                    if lpds != lcf:
                        print(f"LABEL-MISMATCH periods={periods} freq={freq} cal={cal} closed={closed}\n pd={lpds[:6]}\n cf={lcf[:6]}")
                        mismatch += 1
print(f"checked {n} cases, mismatches: {mismatch}")

564	class BinGrouper(Grouper):
565	    """Grouper object for binning numeric data."""
566	
567	    bins: Any  # TODO: What is the typing?
568	    cut_kwargs: Mapping = field(default_factory=dict)
569	    binned: Any = None
570	    name: Any = None
571	
572	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
573	        if duck_array_ops.isnull(self.bins).all():
574	            raise ValueError("All bin edges are NaN.")
575	
576	    def factorize(self, group) -> EncodedGroups:
577	        from xarray.core.dataarray import DataArray
578	
579	        data = group.data
580	
581	        binned, self.bins = pd.cut(data, self.bins, **self.cut_kwargs, retbins=True)
582	
583	        binned_codes = binned.codes
584	        if (binned_codes == -1).all():
585	            raise ValueError(
586	                f"None of the data falls within bins with edges {self.bins!r}"
587	            )
588	
589	        new_dim_name = f"{group.name}_bins"
590	
591	        full_index = binned.categories
592	        uniques = np.sort(pd.unique(binned_codes))
593	        unique_values = full_index[uniques[uniques != -1]]
594	
595	        codes = DataArray(
596	            binned_codes, getattr(group, "coords", None), name=new_dim_name
597	        )
598	        unique_coord = IndexVariable(new_dim_name, pd.Index(unique_values), group.attrs)
599	        return EncodedGroups(
600	            codes=codes, full_index=full_index, unique_coord=unique_coord
601	        )

    t_pd_full = pd.date_range("2000-01-31", periods=periods+4, freq="6h")
    # random-choice sampling patterns to vary regularity
    for pattern in ["regular", "sparse"]:
        if pattern == "regular":
            t_pd = t_pd_full[:periods]

                    if not ok:

                        print(f"MISMATCH n={n_t} {pattern} freq={freq} kw={kw} red={red}: {'; '.join(msgs)}")
print(f"checked {total} cases, {mismatch} mismatches")

import sys, warnings
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

import numpy as np, cftime
from xarray import Dataset, DataArray, date_range

ok = 0
problems = []

def run(tag, time, vals):
    global ok
    for freq in ["Q-DEC","QE-DEC","M","A-DEC","MS","QS-DEC","7D","2QS-OCT"]:
        for kw in [{}, {"closed":"left"}, {"label":"left"}]:
            try:
                ds = Dataset({"pr": ("time", vals)}, coords={"time": time})
                r = ds.resample(time=freq, **kw).mean()
                v = np.asarray(r["pr"].values, float)
                if len(r["time"]) == 0 or not np.all(np.isfinite(v)):
                    problems.append(f"{tag} freq={freq} kw={kw}: BAD result len={len(r['time'])} v={v}")
                else:
                    ok += 1
            except Exception as e:
                problems.append(f"{tag} freq={freq} kw={kw}: EXC {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

# 1) plain object array of cftime datetimes (no CFTimeIndex)
t = np.array([cftime.DatetimeGregorian(1,1,1) + __import__('datetime').timedelta(days=i) for i in range(40)], dtype=object)
run("cftime-object-40", t, np.arange(40.0))

# 2) irregular monotonic cftime
base = cftime.DatetimeGregorian(1,1,1)
gaps = [0,1,2,5,9,14,20,30,45,60,80,100,130,180]
t2 = np.array([base + __import__('datetime').timedelta(days=d) for d in gaps], dtype=object)
run("cftime-irregular", t2, np.arange(len(gaps), dtype=float))

# 3) sub-daily times
base = cftime.DatetimeNoLeap(1,3,15,12,30)
t3 = np.array([base + __import__('datetime').timedelta(hours=6*i) for i in range(100)], dtype=object)
run("cftime-subdaily", t3, np.arange(100.0))

# 4) boundary-aligned starts incl. exact quarter end
for start in [(1,1,1),(1,3,31),(1,4,1),(1,6,30),(1,12,31),(2,1,1)]:
    t4 = np.array([cftime.DatetimeGregorian(*start) + __import__('datetime').timedelta(days=i) for i in range(35)], dtype=object)
    run(f"align-{start}", t4, np.arange(35.0))

# 5) np.datetime64 array coord (non-pandas Index input)
t5 = np.arange(np.datetime64("2001-01-01"), np.datetime64("2001-02-10"), np.timedelta64(1,"D"))
run("dt64-array", t5.astype("datetime64[ns]"), np.arange(40.0))

# 6) min/max on boundary day
t6 = np.array([cftime.Datetime360Day(1,1,30), cftime.Datetime360Day(1,2,1)], dtype=object)
run("edge2", t6, np.array([1.0, 2.0]))

print(f"ok={ok}")
for p in problems[:60]:
    print("PROBLEM:", p)
print("num problems:", len(problems))

events.text: State dependence is subtler — the failing grid reused ONE `Dataset` across iterations. Let me replicate exactly that.

input.command:
python - <<'EOF'
import sys, warnings, traceback
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
sys.path.insert(0, "source/src")
import numpy as np
from xarray import Dataset, date_range

t = date_range(start="0001-01-01", periods=40, freq="D")
ds = Dataset({"pr": ("time", np.arange(40, dtype=float))}, coords={"time": t})
for freq in ["D", "2D", "7D", "h", "12h", "min"]:
    for kw in [{"closed": "right"}, {"closed": "right", "label": "right"}, {"closed": "left"}]:
        try:
            r = ds.resample(time=freq, **kw).mean()
            v = r["pr"].values
            labels = [str(x) for x in r["time"].values]
            print(f"freq={freq} {kw}: len={len(v)}; first labels {labels[:3]}")
            c = ds.resample(time=freq, **kw).count()["pr"].values
            tot = float(np.nansum(c))
            if tot != 40:
                print(f"   !! POINTS LOST: count total={tot} != 40")
            if not np.all(np.isfinite(v)):
                print(f"   !! NONFINITE: {v}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"freq={freq} {kw}: EXC {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

def _construct_boundary_year_date(date_type, *args):
    """Construct a date of type ``date_type``, tolerating boundary years.

    Rolling aggregation windows backwards from dates early in the calendar
    (e.g. computing resample bin edges before a short series that begins in
    year 1) may require dates in year 0.  Calendars that do not support a
    year zero (e.g. ``"standard"`` with ``has_year_zero=False``) reject such
    dates by default.  Construct them explicitly with ``has_year_zero=True``,
    which represents the same instant that more lenient ``cftime`` behavior
    would silently produce for the same arithmetic.
    """
    try:
        return date_type(*args)
    except ValueError as err:
        if "year zero" in str(err):
            return date_type(*args, has_year_zero=True)
        raise


def _normalize_boundary_date(date):
    """Return an equivalent date for out-of-range boundary years.

    Timedelta arithmetic with calendars that do not support a year zero may
    produce dates with negative years (e.g. ``-0001-12-31`` when subtracting
    a day from ``0001-01-01`` on the ``"standard"`` calendar) instead of the
    equivalent year-zero date (``0000-12-31``).  Both forms represent the
    same instant and order identically, but the negative-year form is
    misleading when used as a boundary label (e.g. a resample bin edge).
    """
    if getattr(date, "has_year_zero", True) or date.year >= 0:
        return date
    return type(date)(
        date.year + 1,
        date.month,
        date.day,
        date.hour,
        date.minute,
        date.second,
        date.microsecond,
        has_year_zero=True,
    )


def _days_in_month(date):
    """The number of days in the month of the given date"""
    if date.month == 12:
        reference = type(date)(date.year + 1, 1, 1)
    else:
        reference = type(date)(date.year, date.month + 1, 1)
    return (reference - timedelta(days=1)).day
